evidence: Sen. Ep. 76.5: ‘quantum’ inquis ‘prōficiam?’ quantum temptāveris
Quint. 10.1.112: ille sē prōfēcisse sciat, cui Cicerō valdē placēbit
Caes. BG 7.20: sī nihil in oppugnātiōne oppidī prōfēcisset (Lewis & Short)
Traupman p. 100: ut spērō, prōficimus aliquantum
terms.comment: Of a person’s progress in learning, a skill or a task.

evidence: Cic. Tusc. 3.2: sēmina innāta virtūtum, quae sī adolēscere licēret
terms.comment: Of natural growth: children, plants, and the seeds of a talent.

evidence: Plaut. Pers. 114–115: id tōtum prōcēdit diem
terms.comment: Of how an undertaking goes on.

phrases.latin: sunt enim ingeniīs nostrīs sēmina innāta virtūtum, quae sī adolēscere licēret, ipsa nōs ad beātam vītam nātūra perdūceret
phrases.english: for the seeds of the virtues are born in our nature, and if they were allowed to develop, nature herself would lead us to a happy life
‘how far will I get?’ you ask. As far as you try
We are making some headway, I hope.
